solution: Solution: Mass of sample of alloy $=12\,\text{g}$ $\%$ of metal $X$ in sample $=20$ ∴ If $x$ is the mass of metal $X$ in sample $\frac{x}{12} \times 100 = 20$ $\Rightarrow x = 2.4\,\text{g}$ If $y$ is the mass of metal $Y$ in sample, then $y = 12 - 2.4 = 9.6\,\text{g}$ Number of atoms of X $=\frac{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 2.4}{40}$ $=361 \times 10^{22}$ Ratio of atoms of $X$ and $Y = 2:5$ Number of atoms of $Y = \frac{361 \times 10^{22} \times 5}{2}$ $=9.025 \times 10^{22}$ atoms $9.025 \times 10^{22}$ atoms of $Y$ are present in $9.6\,\text{g}$ . $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ atoms of $Y$ are present in $\frac{95}{9.025 \times 10^{22}} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 64\,\text{g}$ Atomic mass of $Y = 64\,\text{amu}$ . © examsnet.com
